hotspots.title: AfD’s rise and far-right governance threats in Germany
hotspots.blurb: The Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) continues to dominate German political discourse, particularly in Saxony-Anhalt, where it leads polls ahead of the September 6 election. Concerns over its extremist classification and potential governance have sparked debates on financial sanctions and democratic safeguards.
hotspots.affect: This hotspot commands attention due to its high affective investment, combining alarmist framing about extremism, polarized contention over democratic principles, and moral panic over potential governance by a far-right party.

hotspots.title: Lega’s internal rebellion against Salvini’s leadership

hotspots.affect: This hotspot is charged due to its intense intra-party conflict, moral panic over Salvini’s leadership, and polarized contention between regional and national factions, with cross-source repetition amplifying the crisis.

hotspots.title: Vox’s anti-immigration rhetoric and Ceuta crisis
hotspots.blurb: Spain’s far-right Vox party has intensified its anti-immigration rhetoric amid the Ceuta crisis, where thousands of migrants entered the Spanish enclave. Vox demands immediate deportations and accuses the government of enabling human trafficking, sparking polarized contention and moral panic.
hotspots.affect: This hotspot is charged due to its alarmist framing of migration as an existential threat, polarized contention between Vox and the government, and moral panic over crime and cultural erosion, with cross-source repetition amplifying the narrative.
